vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array; when subsequent partition additions reallocate the array, the pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image can trigger this without user interaction, since libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container, which runs no block-device hot-plug management daemon.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires udev/udisks probing a crafted block device on a hot-plug event; the stock container runs no such daemon and performs no block-device management.

analysis.detail: This use-after-free in libblkid's nested partition probing (BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, UnixWare probers) is triggered automatically by udev/udisks as root on a block-device hot-plug event, such as a USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image — containers do not perform hot-plug block-device management, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no invocation of udev, udisks, blkid, or any partition-probing tool; the stock container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships bsdutils 1:2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: util-linux before 2.41.4 has a TOCTOU vulnerability in the SUID /usr/bin/mount binary when setting up loop devices. Exploitation requires an /etc/fstab entry with user,loop options whose path is attacker-writable and a SUID mount binary.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container, which does not provision the required loop-mount configuration for this exploit.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a specific /etc/fstab loop-mount setup that is not configured in the stock Liquibase Secure container.

analysis.detail: This util-linux mount race requires a SUID /usr/bin/mount binary plus an /etc/fstab entry with user,loop options pointing to a user-writable path. The stock Liquibase Secure container's entrypoint only execs a requested command or the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no references to /etc/fstab, /usr/bin/mount, user,loop, blkid, udisks, or udev. The required loop-mount configuration is absent from the stock container.

vulnerabilities.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This image never invokes mount, nsenter, or fstab- driven hooks.

ratings.justification: Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount, nsenter, or reads fstab; single fixed non-root user.

analysis.detail: util-linux fails to check mount helper exit status before running post- mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing files (local privilege escalation on a multi- user host). Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount or nsenter; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user or fstab- controlled surface.

vulnerabilities.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This image never invokes mount, nsenter, or fstab- driven hooks.

ratings.justification: Nothing in this image's runtime calls nsenter; single fixed non-root user.

analysis.detail: nsenter --join-cgroup opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves the descriptor open across later namespace/credential changes and execve() (local privilege escalation). Nothing in this image's runtime calls nsenter; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user surface.

vulnerabilities.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This image never invokes mount, nsenter, or fstab- driven hooks.

ratings.justification: Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount with X-mount.subdir; single fixed non-root user.

analysis.detail: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW that does not stop intermediate symlink traversal (local privilege escalation; Ubuntu rates Medium, upstream CVSS is High at 7.0). Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user surface.

vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This image never invokes mount, nsenter, or fstab- driven hooks.

ratings.justification: Nothing in this image's runtime reads fstab or calls mount; single fixed non-root user.

analysis.detail: Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab without pinning it before the privileged mount, allowing a local unprivileged user to redirect the mount target (local privilege escalation). Nothing in this image's runtime reads fstab or calls mount; the container runs a single fixed non-root user.

vulnerabilities.description: No public advisory text is available yet (NVD/cve.org record not published as of 2026-09-25). Per the Ubuntu util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: a time-of-check-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race in libmount's hook_owner path could allow local privilege escalation during a mount operation; fixed by using fd-based fchownat/chmod instead of path-based calls.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable code (libmount/src/hook_owner.c) ships in the libmount1/mount packages, not bsdutils, and Liquibase Secure never invokes `mount` as part of its application runtime. As defense-in-depth, upgrade to a Secure release built on util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 or later (5.2.2+, which already ships the fixed libmount1/libblkid1/mount packages).

analysis.detail: Scanner package misattribution. No CVE.org, NVD, or Ubuntu security tracker record exists yet for this ID as of 2026-09-25 (NVD totalResults: 0, cve.org returns CVE_RECORD_DNE, and ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-53612 404s), but the util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog (changelogs.ubuntu.com/changelogs/pool/main/u/util-linux) confirms the fix: "Local Privilege Escalation via TOCTOU in mount" -- debian/patches/CVE-2026-53612.patch, "libmount: use fd-based fchownat/chmod in hook_owner", touching libmount/src/hook_owner.c. That file is compiled into the libmount1 shared library and the mount binary package, not bsdutils. Confirmed directly: `dpkg -L bsdutils` inside liquibase/liquibase-secure:5.2.2 lists only logger, renice, script, scriptlive, scriptreplay, and wall -- no mount-related binary or libmount.so. The scanner's SBOM appears to attribute a util-linux-source-package-level fix to every binary package built from that source, including bsdutils, which does not contain the patched code. Even setting misattribution aside, this is a local TOCTOU privilege-escalation bug in a setuid `mount` invocation -- not something Liquibase Secure's headless CLI runtime triggers.

vulnerabilities.description: No public advisory text is available yet (NVD/cve.org record not published as of 2026-09-25). Per the Ubuntu util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: a second TOCTOU race in libmount's mount-context handling could allow local privilege escalation; fixed by tracking the mount target by file descriptor rather than path.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable code ships in the libmount1/mount packages, not bsdutils, and Liquibase Secure never invokes `mount`. As defense-in-depth, upgrade to a Secure release built on util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 or later (5.2.2+).

analysis.detail: Same scanner package misattribution as CVE-2026-53612. No CVE.org, NVD, or Ubuntu security tracker record exists yet as of 2026-09-25. Per the util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: "Another local Privilege Escalation via TOCTOU in mount" -- debian/patches/CVE-2026-53613[-pre1].patch, adding ul_open_no_symlinks() and an fd_target field to libmount's mount context (lib/fileutils.c, libmount/src/context.c, libmount/src/context_mount.c, libmount/src/hook_mount.c, libmount/src/hook_mount_legacy.c) -- all libmount1/mount package files, confirmed absent from bsdutils's file list (`dpkg -L bsdutils` inside liquibase/liquibase-secure:5.2.2: logger, renice, script, scriptlive, scriptreplay, wall only). Same local-TOCTOU- in-setuid-mount threat model as CVE-2026-53612, which Liquibase Secure's headless CLI runtime does not exercise.

vulnerabilities.description: No public advisory text is available yet (NVD/cve.org record not published as of 2026-09-25). Per the Ubuntu util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable could be used to bypass privilege-dropping in the legacy mount(8) code path, allowing local privilege escalation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable code ships in the libmount1/mount packages, not bsdutils, and Liquibase Secure never invokes `mount`. As defense-in-depth, upgrade to a Secure release built on util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 or later (5.2.2+).

analysis.detail: Same scanner package misattribution as CVE-2026-53612/53613. No CVE.org, NVD, or Ubuntu security tracker record exists yet as of 2026-09-25. Per the util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: "Local Privilege Escalation via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 Environment Variable" -- debian/patches/CVE-2026-53614.patch, fixing a SUID bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 in the legacy mount path (libmount/src/hook_mount.c, libmount/src/hook_mount_legacy.c) -- again libmount1/mount package files, confirmed absent from bsdutils's file list. Exploitation requires setting an environment variable ahead of invoking a setuid `mount` binary; Liquibase Secure never invokes `mount` and does not ship a setuid mount binary as part of its own application surface.

vulnerabilities.description: No public advisory text is available yet (NVD/cve.org record not published as of 2026-09-25). Per the Ubuntu util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: a signed integer overflow in libblkid's DOS/MBR extended-partition (EBR) parser (dos.c) could be triggered by a crafted block device, resulting in memory corruption; fixed by validating EBR data and chain links.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable code ships in the libblkid1 package, not bsdutils, and Liquibase Secure never probes block devices or partition tables. As defense-in-depth, upgrade to a Secure release built on util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 or later (5.2.2+).

analysis.detail: Same scanner package misattribution as the other three util-linux CVEs in this batch. No CVE.org, NVD, or Ubuntu security tracker record exists yet as of 2026-09-25. Per the util-linux 2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6 changelog: "Integer Overflow or Wraparound in dos.c" -- debian/patches/CVE-2026-53615.patch, "libblkid: dos: validate EBR data and links within extended partition", touching libblkid/src/partitions/dos.c. That file is compiled into the libblkid1 shared library, not bsdutils -- confirmed absent from bsdutils's file list (`dpkg -L bsdutils` inside liquibase/liquibase-secure:5.2.2: logger, renice, script, scriptlive, scriptreplay, wall only; libblkid1 is a separate installed package). Exploitation requires libblkid to probe a crafted block device's MBR/extended-partition (EBR) table, e.g. via `blkid`/`lsblk`/udev device probing. Liquibase Secure's runtime never probes block devices or partition tables.
